# Lighting, aux fuse blocks and dual batteries

> **Some safety-critical values on this page are not confirmed** (marked [Unverified] or [Partial]): they come from one source or are only partly supported. Verify against the factory service manual before use; later runs re-check them against new sources.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Procedure

1. Install the specified LED bulb into the front signal/running light socket.
2. Check that no hyperflashing occurs during operation.

_Procedure reported by [t174]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t6] [Partial]</summary>

1. Remove the side strip from the passenger kick panel by pulling it with even pressure.
2. Detach the two white pop clips holding the side strip in place.
3. Pop out the two retainers on the side of the truck to free the main kick panel.
4. Pull and release the single retainer located on the floor beneath the panel.
5. Locate three relays inside the cabin that require fuses based on your specific wiring setup.
6. Wrap foam tape around each relay and zip tie them securely in place.
7. Reattach the side kick panel by placing white clips into their retainers.
8. Push down along the entire length of the bottom rail to ensure it is fully clipped in.
9. Drop out the spare tire from the rear of the truck for easier access.
10. Separate the black plug on the driver's rear quarter panel from its mounting location.
11. Route the separated black plug back near the grey factory plug.
12. Remove the protective caps from both the grey and black plugs to expose their contacts.
13. Plug in the corresponding pieces of the new 7-pin wiring harness into the exposed connectors.
14. Zip tie all connected wires together for neatness before routing them along the frame.
15. Secure the cable run using the mounting brackets already attached to the harness kit.
16. Tape off sections of the rear bumper to outline where the receiver will fit.
17. Drill a hole in the marked spot on the bumper using a bi-metal bit at a medium pace with constant pressure.
18. Spray WD40 onto the bumper and drill bit periodically to keep them cool while drilling.
19. Clean up any metal shards from inside and around the fresh hole using a dremel tool.
20. Trim a small section on the right side of the drilled circle if necessary for clearance.
21. Unclip the receiver unit from its connection point on the wiring harness temporarily.
22. Trim the edges on the backside of the receiver to prevent it from hitting surrounding parts.
23. Place the trimmed receiver into the bumper hole and mark the location for the first drill point.
24. Drill out the second hole at the marked position next to the first one.
25. Bolt the receiver securely to the bumper through both drilled holes.
26. Reconnect the wiring harness back onto the mounted receiver.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t761] [Partial]</summary>

1. Remove the trim plate covering the hatch latch by pulling up gently.
2. [Partial] Take out the large tray cover along with its two front screws and three rear screws.
3. Extract the middle piece of trim held between the other two sections.
4. Unscrew the three bolts in the sliding track and pull the track upward.
5. Open a plastic tie-down clip midway up the passenger wall using a flathead tool to remove it.
6. Use a socket to unscrew the rear passenger seat belt's lower bolt.
7. Remove the 10mm bolt located on the wall where the cargo cover attaches.
8. Gently pull the entire wall away from the body starting at the rear while disconnecting the 12V power plug.
9. Lift and work the backrest up and down to free its clips when reaching the seats.
10. [Partial] Run a 2AWG positive wire through the passenger side grommet using a sharpened, straightened wire hanger oriented downward.
11. Remove the front passenger kick panel and lower glovebox to access the interior path for the wires.
12. Tug gently on the wire hanger from inside until most of it is pulled through the grommet area.
13. [Partial] Pull up both front and rear door trims to expose white box channels in each area.
14. Feed the main wire through the exposed channel areas, moving from the front toward the rear under the column with assistance if needed.
15. Follow the stock wiring bundle towards the rear of the vehicle.
16. Create a 2' long section of 6AWG wire for the body ground featuring a lug on one side and a 1/4" lug on the other.
17. [Partial] Bolt the 1/4" end of the new ground wire onto top of the stock OEM ground behind the tail lights.
18. Cut out sections of the hollow passenger-side body metal to make room for the fuse block and switches while avoiding clip locations.
19. [Partial] Cut a hole in the plastic wall specifically sized for the project box installation.
20. Mount the project box using four L-brackets, bending the top brackets back to fit the window sill slope before bolting them with machine screws and nuts.
21. Install screw covers over the mounting points on the project box for aesthetics.
22. Cut out the designated area in the wall for the switch panel and install it into place.
23. Wire all relays and the switch panel into the fuse block, connecting the two yellow load leads from the relays.
24. [Partial] Reattach the wall by feeding both negative wires into the bottom to connect with the negative bus and routing the positive wire from the top to the positive post.
25. [Partial] Replace all removed trim pieces in reverse order of their removal.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t989] [Partial]</summary>

1. Cut an aluminum scrap piece to fit the size of the inverter.
2. Unbolt the crossmember directly below the steering wheel.
3. Drill holes through the upper lip and the aluminum mounting plate.
4. Rivet the two pieces together to secure the mount.
5. Mount one of the power plugs into its location.
6. Solder the ends of a tool replacement cord wire for quick connect utilization.
7. Cut an opening in the dash for the outlet installation.
8. Re-install the upper glove box over the new hole.
9. [Partial] Mount the solenoid onto the relay bracket using self-tapping screws.
10. Attach the power wire from the battery to either side of the solenoid terminal.
11. Connect the ground wire to the solenoid with a self-tapping screw.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t986] [Partial]</summary>

1. Locate the grommet used for the third brake light.
2. Make a straight incision large enough to get the coaxial cable through.
3. Pull back the panel near the hatch and rear side window using a flat head screwdriver.
4. Feed the coaxial cable through the larger hole near the window until there is enough length to reach the roof mount.
5. [Partial] Attach the other end of your cable and pull it tight leaving only a slight amount of slack.
6. Run the coaxial cable along the top of the headliner, removing any metal hooks if necessary for easier routing around the window.
7. Route the cable behind the panel at the seat without pulling that specific panel out completely.
8. [Partial] Continue running the cable along the door seal and up to the headliner before heading down the seal toward the driver side.
9. Pull back the floor panel enough to run the cable through it.
10. Guide the cable across under the weather tech floor mat to reach the side of the driver's chair.
11. Run the cable next to the shifter and pull it around into the cubby hole located under the radio.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t723] [Partial]</summary>

1. Remove the top rack from an oven.

4. [Partial] Use a flathead screwdriver to pry open the edge with no clips while pulling gently.

</details>

## Tips & gotchas

- Use even pressure when pulling the side strip to avoid damage. [t6]
- Drill at a medium pace with constant pressure rather than running too fast. [t6]
- Keep the ground run as short and close to the antenna as possible. [t158]
- Verify continuity between the strap and vehicle ground with a multi-meter. [t158]
- [Partial] Ensure bare metal contact on the stud mount tab, removing paint if necessary. [t158]
- Aim for a flat horizontal metal surface beneath the antenna to create an effective ground plane. [t158]
- Remove all bulbs, rubber grommets, and sockets before baking. [t723]
- Wear gloves as the headlight will be hot when removed. [t723]
- Use glass or eye protection as dirt loves falling into eyes during electrical work. [t985]
- [Partial] Run the main wire path along the frame rail for easy access and neatness. [t985]
- [Partial] Bundle wires tightly together to prevent tangling later on. [t985]
- [Partial] Use existing mounting holes on the air dam to avoid drilling new ones [t1033]
- Consider using an adapter plate to fit a square peg into the round hole [t1033]
- [Partial] Use stock reflectors instead of fabricating new mounting points [t1033]
- [Partial] Choose between HID, LED, or staying stock based on preference [t1033]
- [Partial] Identify which blade is 12V power, output to relay/accessory, and ground for the LED. [t1039]
- Use a friend to help feed the wire from front to rear under the column. [t761]
- Bend back the top L-brackets on the project box to accommodate the slope of the window sill. [t761]
- Use isopropyl alcohol to clean up sharpie marks on the dash. [t399]
- Try Styrofoam first as a spacer before cutting custom pieces. [t399]
- Save space behind the switch pod by consolidating multiple wire runs instead of spreading them out. [t864]
- [Partial] Detach the stereo's faceplate to save space for a tablet. [t929]
- Use liquid electrical tape on soldered connections. [t929]
- Mount the custom holder onto vent tubes for support. [t929]
- [Partial] Connect power via 12V USB adapter in the armrest. [t929]
- Use an application called Tasker on the tablet to automate wake/sleep cycles based on power availability. [t929]
- Control airplane mode via software for better functionality. [t929]
- Use well nuts for a secure base. [t992]
- [Partial] Mount the arm to the left of the 4x4 switch as an ideal spot. [t992]
- [Partial] Look for bulbs with 'can bus ready' features if flickering is a concern. [t174]
- [Partial] Ensure the bulb fits within tight headlight housings without requiring manual clocking. [t174]
- [Partial] Look for bulbs where the white retaining ring is part of a two-piece assembly. [t174]
- [Partial] Check that the fan enclosure diameter clears the headlight's original retainer. [t174]
- Select yellow or white variants based on aesthetic preference versus functional visibility. [t174]
- [Partial] Look for 'can bus' or specific part numbers to avoid battery drain on cheap units. [t174]
- Use these bulbs to create a uniform white look when paired with LED headlights. [t174]
- [Partial] Ensure the unit turns off completely to avoid draining the battery during long sits. [t174]
- [Partial] Consider mounting resistors on a separate bracket if drilling holes in the rust-prone body is undesirable. [t174]
- Check if the bar is 'Made in America' to avoid inconsistent manufacturing quality common with Chinese imports. [t833]
- Be wary of cheap bars that fudge their IPX ratings or list specs that don't apply directly to the unit. [t833]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Using a relay with incorrect amp rating (e.g., 15 amps instead of 10). [t985]
- [Partial] Pulling the coaxial cable too tight after attaching it to the mount [t986]
- [Partial] Forgetting to disconnect the 12V power plug before pulling the wall away, risking a short or blown fuse. [t761]
- Using a low-quality fuse block that had hidden continuity issues rendering fuses useless until after installation. [t761]
- Failing to account for future upgrades like a 4.3-inch mini Din stereo that might need extra clearance behind the switches. [t864]
- [Partial] Using cheap units that leave dome lights dimly lit even when doors are closed. [t174]
- [Partial] Choosing bulbs with external fans that struggle to clear retaining rings in stock headlights. [t174]
- [Partial] Buying a light bar without verifying if it actually has internal potting and solder joints, leading to condensation issues. [t833]
